# CoSec

> Multi-tenant, reactive security framework for Spring Boot (WebFlux, MVC, Spring Cloud Gateway). IAM-style JSON policies and role-based app permissions, evaluated deny-first across global, principal and role layers; JWT authentication; Redis-backed policy storage via CoCache. Kotlin, Java 17, Spring Boot 4, Project Reactor.

Key facts: a DENY matched in any layer overrides any ALLOW; unmatched requests are denied (IMPLICIT_DENY); errors deny. Anonymous denials return 401, authenticated denials 403, exceeded rate limit rules 429. Policies are JSON with `action` (path patterns) and `condition` (single-key objects such as `{"authenticated":{}}`).

## Getting started

- [Introduction](https://cosec.ahoo.me/guide/introduction): what CoSec is, what it decides, the modules and their Gradle capabilities
- [Quick Start](https://cosec.ahoo.me/guide/quick-start): dependency, configuration, first policy, issuing a token, first denied request
- [Concepts](https://cosec.ahoo.me/guide/concepts): principals, tenants, requests, policies and statements, app permissions and roles, decisions
- [Security Model](https://cosec.ahoo.me/guide/security-model): evaluation order, deny-first, default deny, fail closed and its exceptions, tenant isolation, the root principal, hardening checklist

## Integration

- [Web Integration](https://cosec.ahoo.me/integration/web): choosing an adapter (WebFlux, MVC, Gateway), status codes, accessing the security context, app and space headers, client IP behind proxies, request attributes, CORS
- [Authentication](https://cosec.ahoo.me/integration/authentication): JWT tokens, login, refresh, logout and revocation, API keys for machine clients, tenants, social login, the gateway trust boundary
- [Checks in Code](https://cosec.ahoo.me/integration/checks): checking permissions from code (AuthorizationChecker), object-level rules, explaining a decision (cosecExplain)

## Policies

- [Policy Language](https://cosec.ahoo.me/policies/language): reference for every policy field: statements, actions, templates, conditions, expressions, OpenAPI generation, JSON Schema
- [Role Permissions](https://cosec.ahoo.me/policies/role-permissions): app permission catalogs, granting permissions to roles, role grant scope by app and space
- [Rate Limiting](https://cosec.ahoo.me/policies/rate-limiting): rate limit rules and keys, Redis or in-memory counting, 429 and RateLimit headers, failure behavior
- [Testing Policies](https://cosec.ahoo.me/policies/testing): validation, policy test cases, shadow mode, access reviews (AccessAnalyzer)

## Operations

- [Configuration](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/configuration): every `cosec.*` property with its default
- [Storage and Caching](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/storage): local policy files, Redis via CoCache, behavior when Redis is unavailable, publishing changes, policy history and rollback
- [Upgrading](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/upgrading): breaking changes and migration steps per version (6.0 to 6.1, 6.1 to 7.0)
- [Observability](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/observability): audit events, OpenTelemetry tracing, Micrometer metrics, logs
- [Troubleshooting](https://cosec.ahoo.me/operations/troubleshooting): finding what decided, diagnosing 401/403/429/500, policies with no effect, unexpected allows, startup failures, rate limits

## Architecture

- [Overview](https://cosec.ahoo.me/architecture/overview): module layering, request path, authorization decorator chain, invariants and the tests that guard them, caching, startup schema check, performance
- [Extending CoSec](https://cosec.ahoo.me/architecture/extending): custom matchers (SPI), repositories and their contract, authorization hooks, rate limiter backends, shadow providers, context and authentication hooks, audit sinks
